units: <cite ref="Eruvin 77a:12">Erub. 77ᵃ</cite> <he>אם יש במִיעוּטוֹ וכ׳</he> if the reduction of the height (by lowering the wall or raising the embankment) extends over four handbreadths; <he>כנגד המ׳</he> only as far as the reduction extends.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 7:6:3">Y. Pes. VII, 34ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>כרוב או כמ׳</he> (not <he>כרוב׳ במ׳</he>) do we treat the case as if it were a majority (of unclean persons), or as if it were a minority? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 7:6:3">Ib.</cite> <he>אין תימר כמ׳</he> (not <he>במ׳</he>) if you will consider it a minority.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:2:9">Y. Kidd. I, 59ᵇ</cite> top.
<cite ref="Yevamot 119a:9">Yeb. 119ᵃ</cite> <he>מ׳ מפילות</he> a minority of women miscarry; a. e.
R. Hash. 11ᵃ; Yeb. 42ᵃ; Nidd. 38ᵇ (ref. to I Sam. I, 20) מ׳ תקופות וכ׳ the least of t’kufoth (plural number) is two (seasons, of three months each), the least of yamin is two days; a. e.

<cite ref="Yoma 43a:3">Yoma 43ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 86b:19">B. Kam. 86ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>הוי מ׳ אחר מ׳ ואין מ׳ אחר מ׳ אלא וכ׳</he> this is a limitation following a limitation, and a double limitation serves to widen the scope (because the repetition indicates that no limitation is meant, but only an exemplification); Y. Peah V, end, 19ᵈ (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 1:1:2">Y. Hor. I, beg. 45ᶜ</cite> <he>מ׳ אחר מ׳ אחר מ׳</he> three successive limitations.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 24:9">Lev. R. s. 24</cite>, end <he>ת״ל רק לשון מ׳</he> it says ‘only’ (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 28:13">Deut. XXVIII, 13</cite>) which intimates a limitation; a. fr.—Pl. <he>מִיעוּטִים</he>, <he>מִיעוּטִין</he>, <cite ref="M02189"><he>מִע׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Shevuot 1:7">Tosef. Shebu. I, 7</cite> <he>הוה דורש ריבויין ומ׳</he> interpreted the Bible texts with a view to widening and narrowing the limits of the respective laws.
Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵇ אך הוא הרי אלו מ׳ וכ׳ akh and hu (Ex. XII, 16, are limiting qualifications intimating that you must not cut, grind &c. (on the Holy Day).
